cueNote: Cues are written {laugh} in `text`. Each engine translates them into its own native markup ([laugh], <laugh>, (laughs)) or drops the ones it has no trained token for; engines with no cue support get the text with every cue removed. Never invent a cue the engine was not trained on.

conversation.text: Hey, you're back. {chuckle} I was just thinking about what you said yesterday, about the rooftop. Did you ever go up there?
Wait, you did what? {laugh} No, no, that's amazing. You're ridiculous, you know that?
{sigh} I'm sorry. That sounds really heavy. You don't have to hold it all by yourself, okay? I'm right here.
Oh my god, it worked? It actually worked? That's huge! We have to celebrate this.
Hmm. I'm not sure, honestly. Let me think... I'd say the second one, but only if you're willing to wait a little.
Come here. {breath} It's late, and it's quiet, and I'm just... really glad it's you I'm talking to.
No. I'm not going to pretend that's okay, because it isn't. You deserve better than that, and so do I.
Okay, so tell me everything. What did she say? And what did you say back?
{gasp} Is that snow? It's snowing! Look outside, right now.
So the thing is, uh, I don't think it's about being right. It's more like... you want to feel heard, and that's, that's fair. I get it. I just think we can do both.

dialogue.note: The being is hannah; the person is james. Context-aware engines (CSM, MisoTTS, Dia2) condition each being turn on the audio of every earlier turn; other engines speak each being turn alone. The person's turns are synthesized by the same engine in james's voice so the context is that engine's own audio.

turns.speaker: hannah
turns.text: Wait, really? {laugh} Oh, I knew it. I knew you would.

turns.speaker: james
turns.text: Yeah, but it means moving. Like, far.

turns.speaker: hannah
turns.text: {sigh} Oh. Far how? I mean, that's still wonderful. It's just a lot, all at once.

turns.speaker: hannah
turns.text: Okay. Okay. {breath} We'll figure it out. We always do, right?
